newsitem.title: USA: Northridge likely to deliver Brent into NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: Northridge likely to deliver Brent into NYMEX.

text.p: Northridge Energy Marketing Corp has a "strong potential" to deliver one cargo of Brent crude into the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), a trade source familiar with the company's marketing operations said on Tuesday.
Northridge, a subsidiary of TransCanada Pipelines Ltd., "hasn't made a final determination," but seems likely to deliver the 500,000 barrel cargo into the exchange, the source said.
At least one other company was heard to be delivering one million barrels of Nigerian Bonny Light crude into the NYMEX, but this could not be confirmed.
Physical delivery of foreign crude on NYMEX contracts is a rare event as it is usually uneconomic and is considered the option of last resort, traders said.

Exchange for Physical (EFPs) agreements, which allows a buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for physical position, have been fetching a premium of six to 12 cents in recent weeks, as traders rush to escape paper positions that might give them a crude other than the benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing after today's expiry of the May NYMEX contract.

Companies electing to deliver physical crude into the hub at Cushing, Oklahoma can choose to deliver a number of domestic or foreign grades but must give notice to the NYMEX by 1400 EDT/1900 GMT the day after expiry, the source said.
If a company receives Brent instead of WTI, it would receive a fixed discount of 30 cents per barrel to compensate for the differing crude qualities.
Bonny Light would require the company to pay a premium of 60 cents per barrel.
